title: Documentation: ctlv: Describe how to write a family
overview: Adds the driver-API guide for writing a CTLV family: the YAML specification, generated descriptors and callbacks, device lifecycle, operations, hooks, blobs, events and extension through inheritance. It is written against the code of the core (device create/destroy, dispatch, blobs, events) and the generator under tools/ctlv; index.rst and MAINTAINERS wire it into the docs tree and the CTLV entry.

files.purpose: Tutorial-style reference using an invented family, ctlv-example, to walk through every step of implementing a family. Names the generated-code conventions that the generator (tools/ctlv) emits and the core APIs in include/linux/ctlv.h.

units.title: Title and introduction
units.summary: States that a family is a YAML spec plus callbacks named by its generated header, and that CTLV validates requests before callbacks run.
units.details: Points to the userspace ABI document and Documentation/ctlv/specs.

units.title: Registry and generation workflow
units.summary: Explains the three files changed per family and the make targets that regenerate and verify outputs.
units.details: families.yaml is append-only because the index is the family ID baked into attribute and operation IDs. Generation is done by tools/ctlv; generated files must never be hand-edited.

units.title: Write the specification
units.summary: Example YAML: family header, attr-groups (uint, string, blob, nested list) and attr-sets that assemble messages.
units.details: family flags (post-init, pre-fini) select which lifecycle callbacks are generated; attr sets define the required and optional members of a message level, implemented by the schema tables in drivers/ctlv/schema.c.

units.title: Operations in the example spec
units.summary: Declares an optional action, a dynamic query with pre/post hooks, and an event, and states that attribute payload forms are exclusive.
units.details: Types action, query and event correspond to the dispatch in drivers/ctlv core and to event.c; availability: dynamic ties to the disable/enable state.

units.title: Inheritance: parent stub
units.summary: Explains that descendants implement only their own ops and that a parent reserves an extension point with an empty stub set.
units.details: Stubs are the ctlv_stub_schema entries that introspection.c and the validator resolve with ctlv_schema_fill().

units.title: Inheritance: child fill and parent usage
units.anchor: A child fills that same set:
units.summary: Shows a child family filling the stub, the parent opening the nest and calling ctlv_stub_fill(), and the generated fill callback.
units.details: An unfilled stub contributes no nest or length, so neither family names the other.

units.title: Create a device and provider descriptors
units.summary: Shows ctlv_create() with the leaf descriptor and init info, and how pre_init supplies a static descriptor to the parent.
units.details: pre_init runs leaf to root and must return immutable storage or ERR_PTR; the leaf init_info goes only to the leaf's init.

units.title: Creation and destruction order
units.summary: Gives the precise ordering of pre_init, init, freezing of ops, post_init, and the destroy sequence (pre_fini, event drain, fini), including init-failure behaviour.
units.details: Corresponds to ctlv_create()/ctlv_destroy() in the device code; ops are frozen and event admission starts between init and post_init.

units.title: Family privs
units.summary: Describes the per-family priv, and ctlv_priv_parent()/ctlv_priv_child() with their validity at each lifecycle stage.

units.title: Implementing an action
units.summary: Shows an action callback using generated getters and ctlv_op_error().
units.details: Getters read only validated placements; _present() and _for_each() handle optional and repeated attributes.

units.title: Implementing a query
units.summary: Shows a fragmenting query with a generation and cursor, using ctlv_op_query_more/done and -ESTALE.
units.details: Same cursor/generation contract that introspection.c (patch 11) follows; cursors must be nonzero and advance, and each fragment completes a logical leaf.

units.title: Hooks and availability
units.summary: Defines the order of family and operation hooks around a callback and the difference between optional (provide) and dynamic (disable/enable) ops.
units.details: Disabled ops stay discoverable via the ops dump and return -EOPNOTSUPP; state changes emit op-changed.

units.title: Blobs
units.summary: Shows resolving a blob attribute, reading it and releasing it within the callback.
units.details: The schema fixes direction, backing, length and alignment; implemented by blob.c and blob_desc.c.

units.title: Events: emit and abort
units.summary: Shows creating, filling and emitting an event, and the context rules.
units.details: One of emit or abort must end each context; GFP flag covers subscriber copies; no hooks around events. Implemented in event.c.

units.title: Events: reporting a lost event
units.summary: Explains ctlv_event_lost() for events that happened but could not be built, with an example and the accounting it performs.
units.details: It advances event sequence and aggregates into the preallocated EVENT_OVERFLOW record; it neither allocates nor sleeps.

units.title: Reporting an error
units.summary: Distinguishes a callback's errno return from the error information CTLV itself writes into the reply when it rejects a message.

units.title: Configuration
units.summary: Documents CONFIG_CTLV, selected by family implementations.

units.title: Add ctlv to the toctree
units.summary: Registers the new page in the driver-api toctree.

files.purpose: Maintainer database; the CTLV entry already covers the CTLV paths.

units.title: Add the document to the CTLV entry
units.summary: Adds the new driver-api page to the CTLV F: patterns.
